objective: External public-model diagnostic; both branches keep identical lyrics and requested instrumentation. Attribute wording is an intervention, not an artifact label.

cases.style: An intimate indie pop song with female lead vocals, 88 BPM, acoustic guitar, piano, warm electric bass, and live drums. Close-miked human female singing with clear consonants, natural breathing and dynamic phrasing, distinct live-drum attacks and transparent acoustic-guitar and piano detail. Keep the acoustic guitar, piano, electric bass and live drums.
cases.negative_style: An intimate indie pop song with female lead vocals, 88 BPM, acoustic guitar, piano, warm electric bass, and live drums. Robotic, metallic and buzzy female singing with smeared consonants and phasey digital ringing. Keep the acoustic guitar, piano, electric bass and live drums.
cases.lyrics:
[start]
[verse]
Morning light is falling on the avenue
Every quiet window keeps a shade of blue
I can hear the footsteps turning into song
Carry all the small things as we move along
[chorus]
Stay until the city finds a softer glow
Let the little rivers in the streetlights flow
Keep the rhythm breathing as the hours go
There is something here we do not have to know
[verse]
Silver clouds are drifting where the rooftops meet
Someone leaves a flower by the empty seat
Every passing moment has a place to land
We can make a sunrise with an open hand
[chorus]
Stay until the city finds a softer glow
Let the little rivers in the streetlights flow
Keep the rhythm breathing as the hours go
There is something here we do not have to know
[outro]

controls: beta0 pure positive conditional; beta0.5/1 attribute-contrast; same-positive/avoid beta1 sham must match pureconditional PCM under same noise.
limitations: One original lyric set, two instrumentation conditions, one seed; exploratory not generalized control success.
No company renderer/weights or private audio are used.
Acoustic positive/avoid wording does not mention synthesizers; this removes the prior lexical-instrument confound.
Changes in descriptors or production-quality estimates do not prove fewer unwanted artifacts.
